structure.title: Chapter I · News at the courthouse
structure.text: Colleagues learn of Ivan's death and begin to calculate what it means for promotion, condolence visits and an evening at cards. The formal observances are perfectly recognisable. Only afterwards will we get to know the man whose disappearance has disturbed these arrangements.

structure.title: Chapters II–IV · A successful appointment
structure.text: Education, marriage and promotion follow in a brisk retrospective. A new house needs papering and curtains. The small mishap that occurs while Ivan is showing a workman how something should be done belongs thoroughly to the world of tasteful rooms he is determined to build.

structure.title: Chapters V–XII · Time in the sickroom
structure.text: Consultations, visits and efforts to resume work occupy shorter and shorter intervals. Inside the sickroom the hours stretch. Questions about what the doctors call his condition give way to the far less manageable question of why the life he considered correct affords him so little comfort.

people.name: Ivan Ilyich
people.text: Ivan has learned to separate the human beings who appear before him from the legal question he must decide. A specialist now applies an equally polished distinction to him. He finds he urgently needs an answer that falls outside the professional interview.

people.name: Gerasim
people.text: Gerasim does intimate, tiring work other people would rather leave unmentioned. He can acknowledge the approach of death while doing something quite specific to ease pain. His time in the room changes what Ivan can bear to say there.

context.title: Professional courtesy
context.text: The courthouse and the consulting room both have procedures for keeping personal questions out of official business. Politeness also governs family visits. The same forms that once made life agreeably predictable can leave a dying man with nobody who will confirm the plainest fact in the room.

notice.text: Follow the question the doctor answers.
notice.why: Ivan wants to know how grave his situation is. The doctor wants to distinguish between possible diagnoses. Both understand the words being used, yet the conversation shows how two people can leave an interview having discussed different subjects.

notice.text: Watch who is willing to hold a pair of legs.
notice.why: A particular position makes the pain more bearable. Keeping Ivan in it takes strength and time. Against all the assurances offered from the doorway, Tolstoy can set the measurable duration of a servant's physical help.

opening: Ivan Ilyich has arranged his life properly: a respectable career, suitable acquaintances, and a home furnished with the right things. When he becomes seriously ill, the people around him continue observing the conventions that have always made life manageable. Their tact becomes unbearable. Tolstoy brings a successful man into a situation where professional standing and tasteful furniture offer no assistance, and where the question of whether he has lived well becomes urgent before he has learned how to ask it honestly.
